title: Evidence
description: One observation about one property, tied to the content and environment it was made on. Evidence that cannot say what it was measured against is not evidence.

property.description: What is being claimed, in words. Not the command — the claim the command supports.

check.description: The command or procedure actually run.

independent_of.description: Roles whose reasoning this executor did not see. DECLARED by the caller; nothing observes it. Empty means: assume none.

digest.description: The execution context this ran in, comparable without publishing a session id or a pid. Equal digests mean one context.

isolation_signal.description: The recorded dispatch probe the executor's context isolation rests on ("dispatch-probe <date>"), or "none" where no probe was recorded for the harness — and there independent_of is only a declaration.

context.description: MEASURED while the command ran. The counterpart to independent_of, which is not.

fingerprint.description: Digest of the content this run actually exercised: the committed tree plus the uncommitted working tree, excluding the squad's own bookkeeping. A revision alone does not identify content — an uncommitted edit leaves it unchanged, and a --no-ff merge changes it without changing the code.

contract_digest.description: Digest of the Requirements this run was measured against. Evidence about Scenarios cannot speak for Scenarios it never saw.

expected_signal.description: The specific rejection expected. A non-zero exit alone does not satisfy this: a crash also exits non-zero.

expected_tests.description: Pass 1 against a list (--expect-from): the tests that had to fail at their assertion and the preserved regressions that had to pass, in the same run.

limitations.description: What this run did not cover, in the run's own words. A degraded tool says so here.
